entities.summary: Matthew James Perry Jr. was an attorney and in 1979 appointed as the first African-American United States district judge in South Carolina, serving on the United States District Court for the District of South Carolina. In 1976, he had been the first African-American attorney from the Deep South to be appointed to the federal judiciary when he served on the United States Court of Military Appeals. Perry established his career with civil rights litigation, defending Gloria Blackwell in Orangeburg, South Carolina, in her 1962 suit against her arrest for sitting in the whites-only area of the regional hospital while waiting for emergency treatment for her daughter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a civil rights attorney and first African-American judge in South Carolina, Matthew J. Perry played a significant role in advancing racial equality through his work on landmark cases like Gloria Blackwell's suit against her arrest in Orangeburg, SC, and his appointment to the federal judiciary in 1976.
